subject: lavaan 0.6-13 is released on CRAN + bug report

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: lavaan 0.6-13 is released on CRAN + bug report
parts:
Hello all,

lavaan 0.6-13 has been released on CRAN. This is fairly big update with
many changes under the hood. Some 'new' (or finally documented) features
are:

- full support for exploratory factor analysis (EFA), via the efa() function

- a new function lavPredictY() allows for 'prediction' of y-values based
on given (possible out-of-sample) x-values

- a new function lavTest() allows to extract (or compute) one or several
test statistics based on an already fitted object

- 'robust' versions of the RMSEA/CFI are now available for more
settings: when (all) data is categorical/ordered, when data is
continuous but the estimator is MLMV, and when data is incomplete and
missing = “ml” or "fiml" (based on work done by Victoria Savalei and
colleagues)

In addition, a longstanding bug has been found and fixed:

In all lavaan versions < 0.6-13, there was on error in the computation
of scaled (difference) test statistics if (and only if):

1) a mean AND variance adjusted test was used (i.e., test =
“scaled.shifted”, or test = “mean.var.adjusted”),

2) multiple groups were involved, and

3) equality constraints (across groups) were involved.

A typical setting are measurement invariance tests when data is
categorical. In those settings, the resulting test statistic was
slightly off (typically <5%), because the formula used by lavaan was not
correct. Many thanks to Steffen Gronneberg, Njal Foldnes and Jonas Moss
for reporting this.

Yves.


--
Yves Rosseel
Department of Data Analysis, Ghent University

parts:
Thanks a lot for the new features!

May I ask a quick question on the scaled difference test? I posted the following at GitHub and I confirmed that the results are the same for the CRAN 0.6-13:

https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/255

I noticed this actually based on a case with a difference quite large. I failed to locate that case from my computer. So I used the lavaan dataset to create those examples.

Although the p-values are similar, the chi-squares are quite different.

Is it expected and so I should use the result in 0.6-13?

P.S.: I guess my "finding" in the 2nd post (https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/255#issuecomment-1373955318) is irrelevant or coincidental, given the explanation above.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: lavaan 0.6-13 is released on CRAN + bug report
parts:
On 1/12/23 12:03, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:
> I noticed this actually based on a case with a difference quite large.

That could be. If you ever come across a case like that, let me know. It
would be interesting to see under which conditions the difference
becomes large.

Of course, if the value of the test statistic is already very large
relative to the degrees of freedom, it does not matter much. I am mostly
concerned with small values for the test statistic resulting in p-values
close to 0.05, because this may lead to different conclusions.
> Is it expected and so I should use the result in 0.6-13?
To the best of my knowledge, the result in 0.6-13 is correct.

> P.S.: I guess my "finding" in the 2nd post
> (https://github.com/yrosseel/lavaan/issues/255#issuecomment-1373955318)
> is irrelevant or coincidental, given the explanation above.

I agree, although I will still check the role of the scaled.shifted=
argument in lavTestLRT()

Yves.

This is a very welcome update.  I am relatively new to using lavaan.  I will look forward to having robust CFI and RMSEA  available.  Presently, I am unsure which fit measures (e.g., CFI, RMSEA, SRMR) are accurate, scaled or non-scaled when using WLSMV estimator for categorical data. Same for p-value.  And what reasons are the basis for the correct fit measures?  Thank you in advance.


Robert

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: lavaan 0.6-13 is released on CRAN + bug report
parts:
On Friday, January 13, 2023 at 1:24:34 AM UTC+8 @gmail.com wrote:
>Hello Shu Fai,
>On 1/12/23 12:03, Shu Fai Cheung (張樹輝) wrote:
>> I noticed this actually based on a case with a difference quite large.
> That could be. If you ever come across a case like that, let me know. It
> would be interesting to see under which conditions the difference
> becomes large.

I tried to recall what I did and finally came up with a case that have different conclusion. This is a highly artificial case but I think is still worthy of examination.

This is the results from 0.6-13. A two-sample CFA model is fitted. In the second model, a factor covariance is fixed to zero:

# Adapted from https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-13
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
set.seed(65145)
dat <- HolzingerSwineford1939
dat <- dat[sample(nrow(dat), 200), ]

# No between group constrains
HS.model1 <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~~ textual
              visual ~~ speed
              textual ~~ speed'
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model1,
           data = dat,
           group = "school",
           meanstructure = TRUE,
           test = "satorra.bentler",
           check.start = FALSE)

HS.model2 <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~~ textual
              visual ~~ c(0, NA) * speed
              textual ~~ speed'
fit2 <- cfa(HS.model2,
           data = dat,
           group = "school",
           meanstructure = TRUE,
           test = "satorra.bentler",
           start = fit1,
           check.start = FALSE)

parameterestimates(fit1)[11, ]
#>       lhs op   rhs block group   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 11 visual ~~ speed     1     1 0.191 0.098 1.955  0.051   -0.001    0.384
parameterestimates(fit2)[11, ]
#>       lhs op   rhs block group est se  z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 11 visual ~~ speed     1     1   0  0 NA     NA        0        0

lavTestLRT(fit2, fit1, method = "satorra.2000")
#>
#> Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.2000")
#>
#> lavaan NOTE:
#>     The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the
#>     robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference
#>     test is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.
#>  
#>      Df    AIC    BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)  
#> fit1 48 5008.1 5206.0 109.64                                
#> fit2 49 5010.6 5205.2 114.14     4.8927       1    0.02697 *
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

This is the result from 0.6-12:

# Adapted from https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html
library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-12
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
set.seed(65145)
dat <- HolzingerSwineford1939
dat <- dat[sample(nrow(dat), 200), ]

# No between group constrains
HS.model1 <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~~ textual
              visual ~~ speed
              textual ~~ speed'
fit1 <- cfa(HS.model1,
           data = dat,
           group = "school",
           meanstructure = TRUE,
           test = "satorra.bentler",
           check.start = FALSE)

HS.model2 <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
              visual ~~ textual
              visual ~~ c(0, NA) * speed
              textual ~~ speed'
fit2 <- cfa(HS.model2,
           data = dat,
           group = "school",
           meanstructure = TRUE,
           test = "satorra.bentler",
           start = fit1,
           check.start = FALSE)

parameterestimates(fit1)[11, ]
#>       lhs op   rhs block group   est    se     z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 11 visual ~~ speed     1     1 0.191 0.098 1.955  0.051   -0.001    0.384
parameterestimates(fit2)[11, ]
#>       lhs op   rhs block group est se  z pvalue ci.lower ci.upper
#> 11 visual ~~ speed     1     1   0  0 NA     NA        0        0

lavTestLRT(fit2, fit1, method = "satorra.2000")
#> Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.2000")
#>
#> lavaan NOTE:
#>     The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the
#>     robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference
#>     test is a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.
#>  
#>      Df    AIC    BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)  
#> fit1 48 5008.1 5206.0 109.64                                
#> fit2 49 5010.6 5205.2 114.14     3.8339       1    0.05023 .
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

The p-value of the LR test is .02697 in 0.6-13 and 0.05023 in 0.6-12.

All other results are the same. Therefore, I think the difference is due to the scaling and shift factors.

I artificially created this case by trying different subsets of the data. However, the scenario is not unusual. It compares two CFA models, testing the impact of fixing a covariance (correlation) to one.

Hope this case is useful for understanding the adjustment.

-- Shu Fai
